## Vocabulary

Terms this pack was harvested with, grouped by their relation to the concept; counts are units matched / sources. Zero-hit terms are listed under Coverage. On every unit line, `keywords:` names the terms that matched.

- **self**: Salesforce single-subscriber durable MongoDB alert distribution (16/3)

## Definitions

- [statement] Replay position is not a universal event deduplication key: Salesforce says replay IDs can repeat during maintenance. Its event id identifies platform events, but that field is absent on change events. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/event-message-durability.html · keywords: Salesforce single-subscriber durable MongoDB alert distribution

## How it works

- [statement] For proposed per-instance fanout, each application instance can open its own collection change stream and serve its connected clients. Budget database connections for those watchers: each active stream holds a connection while waiting, and exceeding the connection pool can cause notification latency. This proposal does not establish competing-consumer or per-client delivery acknowledgments. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/changestreams/ · keywords: Salesforce single-subscriber durable MongoDB alert distribution

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Avoid opening an independent MongoDB change stream for every browser session without capacity planning. Each active stream holds a connection while waiting, and exceeding the connection pool can add notification latency. Sharing streams through application distributors is a design inference. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/changestreams/ · keywords: Salesforce single-subscriber durable MongoDB alert distribution

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Design inference: when the inbox record and ingest checkpoint occupy separate MongoDB documents, commit them together in a transaction with suitable read and write concerns. Advance the checkpoint only after durable acceptance, so a restart cannot skip work that existed only in memory. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md · keywords: Salesforce single-subscriber durable MongoDB alert distribution · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/change-streams/change-streams.md, https://github.com/meyc-v1/wolverinefxcontrib-salesforcepubsub
- [statement] A MongoDB resume token cannot recover changes after its required oplog history has disappeared. Therefore treat change streams as a live notification mechanism and retain queryable alert records for application recovery beyond that history window; this retention recommendation is a design inference. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/changestreams/ · keywords: Salesforce single-subscriber durable MongoDB alert distribution · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/docs/change_streams.md, https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/change-streams/change-streams.md
- [statement] Automatic driver recovery does not replace application recovery: the MongoDB specification requires one resume attempt after a resumable error, while the manual says a driver throws if it cannot find a node with the correct read preference. (high confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/change-streams/change-streams.md · keywords: Salesforce single-subscriber durable MongoDB alert distribution · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/changestreams/
- [statement] Proposed collector backpressure: request Salesforce events according to durable MongoDB commit throughput and bound in-flight work. Subscribe supports pull-based flow control based on processing speed; MongoDB transactions commit results or end on error. (medium confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html · keywords: Salesforce single-subscriber durable MongoDB alert distribution · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Salesforce CUSTOM replay resumes after the supplied position. Store replay IDs as opaque bytes rather than incrementing them or assuming they are numeric. (medium confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html · keywords: Salesforce single-subscriber durable MongoDB alert distribution · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/event-message-durability.html

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Design inference: use one upstream Salesforce subscription to ingest into a persistent MongoDB inbox, then let application distributors read committed database changes. The cited APIs provide the building blocks; they do not certify this combined architecture or require a single subscriber. (medium confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html · keywords: Salesforce single-subscriber durable MongoDB alert distribution · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/changestreams/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md
- [statement] Salesforce retains platform and change-data-capture events for 72 hours. Use replay for temporary disconnect recovery; it does not provide an unlimited downstream alert archive. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/event-message-durability.html · keywords: Salesforce single-subscriber durable MongoDB alert distribution · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html
- [statement] MongoDB change streams notify only after changes have persisted to a majority of data-bearing replica-set members; this database durability boundary does not itself acknowledge application processing. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/changestreams/ · keywords: Salesforce single-subscriber durable MongoDB alert distribution · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/change-streams/change-streams.md
- [statement] Application processing must tolerate redelivery. The MongoDB driver specification assigns idempotency to the application; the Wolverine Salesforce transport illustrates a durable inbox that persists before processing and deduplicates by event identity. Its example is platform-event-specific and is not proof of a MongoDB or Case CDC implementation. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/change-streams/change-streams.md · keywords: Salesforce single-subscriber durable MongoDB alert distribution · also: https://github.com/meyc-v1/wolverinefxcontrib-salesforcepubsub
- [statement] Resume a MongoDB change stream with the pipeline and options that produced its token. Changing the filter can exclude the resume event and prevent recovery. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/docs/change_streams.md · keywords: Salesforce single-subscriber durable MongoDB alert distribution · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/changestreams/
- [statement] Proposed distribution pattern: use one Salesforce collector to persist alert records and its processed-event checkpoint in one MongoDB transaction; downstream application instances consume MongoDB notifications. This combines documented primitives and is an architectural recommendation, not a vendor-provided end-to-end exactly-once guarantee. (medium confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/event-message-durability.html · keywords: Salesforce single-subscriber durable MongoDB alert distribution · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/changestreams/
- [statement] Keep durable alert documents as the recovery source and use change streams to wake downstream readers: MongoDB describes notification services as a change-stream use case and emits notifications only after majority persistence. This is a proposed alert-distribution design. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/changestreams/ · keywords: Salesforce single-subscriber durable MongoDB alert distribution
- [statement] Persist alert effects before advancing the processed Salesforce checkpoint. If a crash leaves the checkpoint behind, replay may repeat work; make alert creation and downstream effects idempotent. This ordering is a design inference from Salesforce processed-event replay and MongoDB transaction and consumer guidance. (medium confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/event-message-durability.html · keywords: Salesforce single-subscriber durable MongoDB alert distribution · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md, https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/change-streams/change-streams.md

## Research summary — Salesforce single-subscriber durable MongoDB alert distribution

A proposed distribution architecture uses one Salesforce subscription to persist an inbox in MongoDB, then distributes application alerts from committed database changes. Salesforce replay supports recovery within a finite retention window. MongoDB transactions can couple durable intake with checkpoint updates, while change streams supply live notifications. Neither replay positions nor notifications establish exactly-once application delivery. Consumers need idempotent processing, and alert records must remain queryable when change-stream history is unavailable. The combined architecture is a design inference from vendor primitives; the cited Wolverine repository supplies an analogous durable Salesforce inbox for platform events, not a MongoDB Case implementation.
